name: BankToCustomerStatement
label: Bank To Customer Statement
summary: The formal end-of-day account statement: opening and closing balances, and every booked entry in between. The system of record a customer reconciles against.
whenUsed: Delivered once per account per business day, after the books close. Legally and operationally the authoritative statement — intraday views come from camt.052 and must never be treated as final. Replaces MT940 (customer statement) and MT950 (bank-to-bank statement).
gotchas: Only booked entries appear here. Pending items live in camt.052. A customer comparing a camt.052 total against a camt.053 total and finding a difference has usually found this distinction, not an error.
Amounts are unsigned — the direction is in CdtDbtInd. Summing Amt without reading the indicator produces a number that looks plausible and is wrong.

The booked balances must reconcile: OPBD plus the signed sum of entries equals CLBD. If they do not, you have dropped an entry or double-counted a reversal. Available balance (CLAV) will not reconcile this way and is not supposed to.
Statement sequence numbers matter. ElctrncSeqNb increments per account; a gap means a statement you never received, and silently ignoring gaps is how reconciliations drift for weeks.

fields.name: Message Recipient
fields.note: Who the statement is addressed to, where that is not the account owner — e.g. a shared service centre.

fields.name: Message Pagination
fields.note: Page number and last-page indicator. Large accounts are split across messages, and processing only page one is a real failure mode.

fields.name: Statement
fields.note: One per account per period. A single message can carry statements for many accounts.

fields.name: Electronic Sequence Number
fields.note: Increments per account per statement. Track it and alarm on gaps.

fields.name: Legal Sequence Number
fields.note: The paper statement's number, which may advance at a different rate from the electronic one.

fields.name: From To Date
fields.note: The period covered. Essential for detecting both gaps and overlaps between statements.

fields.name: Copy Duplicate Indicator
fields.note: Marks a reissued statement. Loading a DUPL as though it were new double-books every entry.

fields.name: Account
fields.note: Which account this is.

fields.name: Account Currency
fields.note: The account's own currency. Entries may be in others, with the conversion in AmtDtls.

fields.name: Account Servicer
fields.note: The bank holding the account.

fields.name: Balance
fields.note: Repeating, and you must read the type of each. A statement typically carries OPBD, CLBD and CLAV at minimum.

fields.name: Balance Amount
fields.note: Unsigned. Read with the indicator below.

fields.name: Credit Debit Indicator
fields.note: DBIT on a balance means the account is overdrawn.

fields.name: Transactions Summary
fields.note: Counts and totals of credit and debit entries. A cheap integrity check against your own parsed figures.

fields.name: Entry
fields.note: One booked movement. The MT940 :61: line, with structure.

fields.name: Amount
fields.note: In the account's currency unless stated otherwise. Unsigned.

fields.name: Reversal Indicator
fields.note: True means this entry reverses an earlier one. Crucially, the amount stays positive and the indicator flips — so a reversal of a credit is a DBIT entry with RvslInd true. Miss this and reversals double-count.

fields.name: Status
fields.note: BOOK for booked, PDNG for pending, INFO for informational. In a camt.053 this should be BOOK.

fields.name: Booking Date
fields.note: When the entry hit the books.

fields.name: Value Date
fields.note: When it counts for interest and availability. Differs from booking date for cheques and cross-border credits, which is exactly where float lives.

fields.name: Account Servicer Reference
fields.note: The bank's own reference. The value to quote when querying an entry.

fields.name: Bank Transaction Code
fields.note: A four-level classification — domain, family, sub-family — that says what kind of movement this is. Replaces the MT940 two-letter transaction type and is what lets you classify entries without string-matching narratives.

fields.name: Domain Code
fields.note: PMNT for payments, ACMT for account management, FORX for FX, SECU for securities.

fields.name: Family Code
fields.note: e.g. RCDT for received credit transfers, ICDT for issued credit transfers, RDDT for received direct debits.

fields.name: Sub Family Code
fields.note: e.g. ESCT for a SEPA credit transfer, DMCT for a domestic one, RRTN for a returned payment.

fields.name: Proprietary
fields.note: The bank's own transaction code. Often more granular than the ISO code, and always less portable.

fields.name: Charges
fields.note: Fees applied to this entry, itemised rather than netted into the amount.

fields.name: Entry Details
fields.note: Where a batch entry is broken out into its components. A single aggregated payroll debit expands here into its individual payments.

fields.name: Batch
fields.note: Identifies the originating batch — carries back the PmtInfId from your pain.001.

fields.name: Transaction Details
fields.note: The individual underlying payment. This is the part MT940 simply could not express.

fields.name: References
fields.note: All the identifiers from the original payment, preserved.

fields.name: End To End Identification
fields.note: The reference the payer set. The single most valuable element in the whole statement for automated reconciliation.

fields.name: UETR
fields.note: Lets a statement entry be tied back to a tracked payment.

fields.name: Mandate Identification
fields.note: For direct debit entries — which mandate was used.

fields.name: Amount Details
fields.note: Instructed amount, counter-value, and the exchange rate applied — how you explain why a 10,000 EUR invoice credited as 16,420 AUD.

fields.name: Charges
fields.note: Deductions taken from this specific payment, which is how a creditor finally sees why it received less than the invoice.

fields.name: Related Parties
fields.note: Structured debtor and creditor, rather than a name buried in narrative text.

fields.name: Debtor Account
fields.note: The paying account. Needed for matching when the payer's reference is useless.

fields.name: Ultimate Debtor
fields.note: Who the payment was really from, where a platform or agent paid on their behalf.

fields.name: Remittance Information
fields.note: What the payer said the payment was for.

fields.name: Structured Remittance Information
fields.note: Invoice-level detail, where the payer sent it and the chain preserved it.

fields.name: Return Information
fields.note: Present when the entry is a returned payment — carries the return reason code, so you learn why without raising a query.

fields.name: Additional Entry Information
fields.note: The bank's free-text narrative. Where legacy MT940 text tends to end up — useful to a human, poor input for automation.
